operator_question: Summer Apparel sell-through is collapsing — units down 22% week-on-week, categorical overstock visible. Build a markdown + push plan that doesn't blow margin floors and explain how stores rebalance.
findings_md:
- summer_apparel sell-through fell 22% WoW with 1,840 units on hand category-wide.
- SUM-001 (320 on hand) and SUM-002 (410 on hand) account for the largest exposure; both at <0.45 30-day sell-through.
- Margin floor is 0.20; price floor at $32 caps any flat-percentage cut at ~30%.
evidence_md:
| metric | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| sell_through_wow | -0.22 | aggregate_by_category(category='summer_apparel') |
| on_hand_units | 1,840 | inventory_health(category='summer_apparel') |
| margin_floor | 0.20 | list_categories — policy table |
| top SKU on-hand | SUM-001=320, SUM-002=410 | aggregate_by_category top-sku slice |
open_questions_md:
- Is the 22% drop concentrated in one store cluster, or category-wide?
- Are any inbound POs in flight that would reset the overstock math after a markdown?

operator_question: Heatwave hits this weekend. Push the right summer categories and lock down the campaign budget. I need this in market within 24h.
findings_md:
- Heatwave window is ~72h; summer_apparel (sensitivity 0.85) and hydration (0.72) are the two categories that lift in this regime.
- $47k remains under the $65k weekly budget cap after $18k already committed across 3 open campaigns.
- 24h time-to-market is tight; existing campaign creative for summer_apparel can ship same-day, hydration would need new creative.
evidence_md:
| metric | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| weather_signal | heatwave_72h | get_kpis() |
| top sensitivity | 0.85 (summer_apparel) | list_categories() |
| budget remaining | $47,000 | list_campaigns() — committed vs cap |
open_questions_md: - Is hydration's creative reusable from the last heatwave campaign, or does it need a new brief?

operator_question: BreezeCo and SunGoods are flagged in the supplier risk panel. Two inbound POs in the next 10 days. Should we hold them, expedite them, or split the call by vendor?
findings_md:
- BreezeCo PO-441: 4 days out, on-hand has 11 days runway — holding is safe; lateness risk is the primary driver.
- SunGoods PO-447: 9 days out, on-hand has only 5 days runway — holding creates a stockout window. Damage risk is the driver, so partial inspection-on-arrival is the cleanest split.
- Vendor-by-vendor call: hold BreezeCo, expedite SunGoods.
evidence_md:
| po_id | vendor | days_out | runway | risk_driver |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PO-441 | BreezeCo | 4 | 11 | lateness |
| PO-447 | SunGoods | 9 | 5 | damage |

Source: inventory_health().inbound_pos
open_questions_md: - What's the cost delta of expediting SunGoods vs accepting a 4-day stockout window?

operator_question: Store-3 is stocked out on SUM-002. Local demand is high. What's the right play — transfer from another store, ship from DC, or pivot to BOPIS with a different SKU substitute?
findings_md:
- Store-3 demand is ~60 units over 7 days; SUM-002 is out.
- store-2 has 110 on-hand and labor_pressure 0.3 — lowest-pressure store with surplus. Transferring 50 units leaves it with 60 (still above its own 7-day demand of ~45).
- store-4 has only 40 on-hand at labor_pressure 0.8 — pulling from it would create a second stockout under load.
- BOPIS pivot to a substitute (SUM-001, similar category) is feasible if transfer ETA is >24h.
evidence_md:
| store | on_hand | labor_pressure |
|---|---|---|
| store-1 | 90 | 0.7 |
| store-2 | 110 | 0.3 |
| store-4 | 40 | 0.8 |
| store-5 | 75 | 0.5 |

Source: get_kpis().store_inventory + substrate_stores
open_questions_md:
- Is BOPIS demand history showing operators accept SUM-001 as a SUM-002 substitute?
- What's transfer ETA from store-2 to store-3 in the current routing model?
